schemes.official_name: Engineering Projects in Community Service (EPICS) at Purdue
schemes.description: Multi-semester student teams design, build and deploy engineering-based systems for community service and education organisations in four areas: human services, access and abilities, education and outreach, environment.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: All undergraduates; senior design route requires approval (email epics@purdue.edu)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Open to all undergraduates; senior-design registration needs prior approval
schemes.credit_assessment: Variable credit 1-3 per semester (search summary of syllabus; not confirmed on fetched page); credit applied to major by department/advisor
schemes.duration: Minimum two consecutive semesters; multiyear partnerships; 2-hour weekly lab
schemes.project_evidence: Teams 'design, build, and deploy real systems' for partners [1]; multiyear projects.
schemes.group_evidence: Student teams; recommended team size 8-20 mixing years and majors [3, search-index summary of EPICS about/syllabus pages, not opened].
schemes.employer_evidence: 'Each team has a multiyear partnership with a community service or education organization'; teams build projects 'for real community organizations' [1][2]. External organisations, not internal units.
schemes.partner_role: Community/education organisation partner defines project need and receives the deployed system; partners typically not-for-profit, also schools and government groups (search summary)
schemes.named_partners: Habitat for Humanity Lafayette (search summary, undated)
schemes.unresolved: Credit hours and team size come from a search-index summary, not an opened page.

profile_md: Purdue shows several distributed team-with-external-partner routes. EPICS is the strongest institution-wide route: open to all undergraduates, multi-semester teams (reported 8-20 students) build systems for community, education and government partners; Spring 2027 registration confirmed. The Data Mine Corporate Partners (any major) runs year-long Agile teams with industry mentors (90+ projects, 68 partners in 2025), but no 2025/26+ dated source was found. The Daniels School of Business Office of Business Partnerships embeds company-defined team projects in named MGMT courses (labelled up to 2026), with presentations to company leadership. Boiler Communication (COM 49101) is a student-run PR agency class whose teams serve external non-profit and business clients. Engineering departments (IE, ME, Polytechnic) host sponsored senior capstones, but group structure and sponsor roles were verified only for part. CS 44100 is partner-sponsored only in some projects. Not verified: dated currency of Data Mine and Boiler Communication, compulsory status of capstones, participation counts.
gaps: Further departmental engineering capstones (ME463, NE, BME, MDE, Polytechnic ET) likely; business partner page read only to first 100k characters; EPICS credit/team size from search summary; Data Mine and Boiler Communication lack 2025/26-2026/27 dating. Only one query each for science and other areas.
